issues.description: Field Farm.animals: problem statement UML declares an attribute animals: List<Animal> (UML), while the textual instructions later require the Farm to use a Set (HashSet) to ensure uniqueness. The UML (animals: List<Animal>) appears at the UML class block, whereas the textual description (use Set / HashSet, unique animals) appears in the Part 3 Farm task. This contradiction leaves students unsure whether to implement Farm.animals as a List or a Set, which affects the field type, constructor initialization, and the getter/setter signatures.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type consistent in the problem statement. Either (A) update the UML to show animals: Set<Animal> (and mention HashSet in the UML notes) so both UML and textual instructions require a Set, or (B) remove the Set/HashSet requirement from the textual Farm task and keep List<Animal> in both the UML and text. Ensure the constructor and getter/setter in the template/solution match the chosen collection type.

issues.description: Field Farm.animals type mismatch between specification and reference solution: the textual specification in the problem statement requires Farm.animals to be a Set (HashSet) to enforce uniqueness, but the solution implementation declares private List<Animal> animals and initializes it with an ArrayList. This causes the reference solution to diverge from the specification and confuses students trying to compare their implementations to the provided solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution repository with the problem specification or vice versa. Preferred resolution: change the solution to use a Set<Animal> (e.g., private Set<Animal> animals = new HashSet<>();), update the getter/setter signatures to Set<Animal>, and keep addAnimal(Animal) behavior the same but rely on the Set to avoid duplicates. Alternatively, if Lists are to be allowed, update the problem statement to accept List<Animal> and remove the explicit HashSet requirement.
